memory_update.text: DSGX is the cleanest US-listed software/data candidate for the supply-chain intelligence and compliance-tools node because its Global Trade Intelligence products map directly to sanctions screening, customs compliance, tariff/duty workflows, and trade-record visibility.

ULS should be retained as the TIC reference anchor for testing, inspection, certification, supplier audits, responsible sourcing, and regulatory/supply-chain software, despite being larger than the preferred underfollowed range.

MG is a low-attention small-cap candidate for inspection/testing capacity tied to aerospace, defense, power, infrastructure, and industrial supplier qualification; needs proof that growth is not just legacy oil & gas asset-integrity demand.

SPIR remains only a speculative-shadow vessel-tracking candidate after selling its maritime business to Kpler; verify retained government maritime revenue and any ongoing Kpler/data relationship before advancing.

Important private or non-US-listed context names include Kpler, Altana AI, Lloyd's List Intelligence, Intertek, SGS, Bureau Veritas, and Dun & Bradstreet after its 2025 take-private transaction; they help map the node but are not US-listed candidates for this pass.

node: Supply-chain intelligence, vessel tracking, compliance, certification, and inspection tools
summary: Layer 1B expands the public-stock universe around the information and verification layer that may benefit when route-dependent supply shocks, export bans, tariffs, forced-labor rules, sanctions, defense procurement rules, and critical-material shortages raise demand for trade intelligence, vessel visibility, customs/origin compliance, inspection, and certification. The strongest US-listed fits found in this pass are not commodity producers but software/data and TIC/inspection vendors. Descartes and UL Solutions are the cleanest public mappings; MISTRAS and Spire are underfollowed or speculative-shadow mappings that need sharper revenue-exposure verification.
